post.description: Rotate a key: revoke the old one, create a new one with same settings.

Probe a model to check for live internet/web-search access.

Detection uses a nonce-based approach: a unique token is embedded in the
prompt and the model must echo it back.  Only a model with real-time web
access can retrieve today's date from an external source AND return the
exact nonce — a model that merely repeats the prompt cannot satisfy both
constraints simultaneously.

By default the result is **not** persisted to providers.json.  Pass
``"persist": true`` in the request body to save ``internet_access`` for
the model.  Name-based heuristics (kimi, glm …) are intentionally absent;
the decision is driven solely by the actual response.

Bulk-probe every active model for live internet access.

Iterates over every model returned by ``list_models()`` and calls
:func:`check_model_internet_access` with bounded concurrency
(``PLUGBOARD_BULK_INTERNET_CONCURRENCY``, default 3). A single global
lock prevents two bulk runs from overlapping — a second concurrent call
returns 409.

Pass ``"persist": true`` (default ``false``) to write ``internet_access``
back into ``providers.json`` for each tested model. Pass ``"provider":
"<provider_id>"`` to restrict the scan to one provider. Pass
``"skip_local": true`` to leave local Ollama models out (the boot probe
does): they have no web access, and probing one makes the host load and
run it. Ollama Cloud models are still probed.

Trigger a synchronous connectivity re-probe for all active providers.

Blocks until complete (timeout: 120s). Returns the updated status.
A 60-second cooldown (configurable via PLUGBOARD_REFRESH_COOLDOWN_S)
prevents sequential spam: repeated calls within the cooldown window
receive HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.

get.description:
Liveness (PLU-31): always 200 while the process answers. Public, so it
shows the status and the version only and reads no file; the provider
list is on the admin `GET /providers`, the auth posture on
`GET /health/ready`.

Detailed health check — probes every active provider.

Uses the same probe as the dashboard Ping (health_probe.probe_provider):
CLI providers are checked through their binary, local servers through
the URL they really serve, and the provider's credentials are sent.

Readiness (PLU-31): 200 when this instance can serve requests, 503
otherwise. Public: a load balancer reads the status code with no key.

The body is ``ready`` and ``version``; ``checks`` (generic states: which
check failed, the client auth posture) is added for a valid key only
(PLU-75): an active client key, the admin key (no TOTP: a read of
generic states) or an admin session, a person's session included; a
bare personal key (``pba_``), even with its code, gets no checks
(PB-AUTH-01). A wrong, forged or revoked key is
not refused here: it gets the same body as no key. With both API_KEY and
ADMIN_KEY empty every route is open (loopback only), so are the checks.

post.description:
Discover a provider's models and write them; removals apply at once.

``dry_run=true`` returns what would be added and removed without writing,
so the dashboard can ask for confirmation first. A call from the MCP
server is audited with its refusals and previews (PB-MCP-02).

get.description:
Identities listed in PLUGBOARD_EMBEDDING_MODELS this key may use.

Unregistered owners and identities the key may not use are left out.
``available`` says whether the route resolves (owner registered, active,
loopback local engine); it does not probe the engine. ``dimensions`` is
known once a call was served since the last restart, else null.

Chat calls in flight and the last results (PLU-13).

calls only, without routing details.

post.description:
Smoke-test a batch of provider+model pairs before a long benchmark.

Each ping goes through the chat admission checks (allowed_models, budget,
a provider that is not turned off, a model some provider knows, known
price, rpm) and is billed like a chat call. The batch holds one slot of
the global cap, given back while a ping waits for a full provider and
taken back right before a provider is called (BUG-77, PLU-51): a pair it
cannot ping for want of a slot answers ``server_busy``. Errors are closed codes, never the
provider's text.

OAuth redirect callback (Authorization Code flow).

Public endpoint (not admin-protected) — CSRF-protected via state token.
Exchanges the code for tokens and returns an HTML page that closes
the popup and notifies the parent via postMessage.

Security: every interpolated value is html-escaped for the body and
json-encoded for the postMessage payload. The target origin is pinned
to the current server origin instead of "*" so a hostile parent page
that opened the popup cannot intercept the message.

otpauth:// provisioning URI. Nothing is persisted yet — the caller must
confirm with /admin/mfa/setup and a valid code from their authenticator.

routes.description:
Step 2 of enrolment: the admin submits the secret from /begin plus a
code read from their authenticator app. On success the secret is

TOTP codes once PLUGBOARD_ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED=1. Replacing an enrolled
secret also needs a current code from it (``current_code``).

is enrolled (lost authenticator: scripts/admin_mfa_setup.py --rotate on
the host).
